launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.address: 900 Druid Park Lake Drive, Baltimore, MD 21217
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.summary: Baltimore's landmark 745-acre city park, combining Druid Lake, Rawlings Conservatory, the Maryland Zoo, pool, playgrounds, disc golf, pavilions, wooded routes and the Jones Falls Trail.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.hours: Outdoor park areas are generally available from dawn to dusk. Rawlings Conservatory, the Maryland Zoo, pool, recreation facilities and permitted events keep separate schedules; check the exact destination before visiting.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.parking: Parking is distributed around this very large park. Navigate to Rawlings Conservatory, the zoo, pool, Chinese Pavilion or another named destination rather than relying on the general park pin; construction and events can change internal roads.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.arrival: The park spans multiple entrances and cannot be treated as one compact stop. Madison Avenue is useful for the conservatory and lake side, while zoo, pool and western recreation areas require their own approach.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.restrooms: Dependable restrooms are tied to staffed attractions, the pool and active recreation facilities. Remote lawns, trails and pavilions may not have an unlocked restroom nearby.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.cost: General park, lake-loop and trail access are free. Zoo admission, pool entry, golf, programs, rentals and reservable pavilions cost separately.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.accessibility: The lake loop and major facility approaches include paved routes, but wooded trails, historic slopes and older pavilion areas vary. Use the closest destination parking for a shorter step-free approach.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor park areas. Dogs are not permitted inside the zoo, conservatory, pool or other posted facilities except qualified service animals.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.family: The zoo, conservatory, playgrounds and seasonal pool are strong family destinations, but they are spread apart. Choose a primary stop and confirm that facility's tickets, hours and weather status.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.transit: MTA bus routes serve different edges of Druid Hill Park, and the Jones Falls Trail reaches the park by bike and foot. The nearest stop may still be a long walk from the attraction you selected.
launch-md-baltimore-druid-hill-park.need: Do not swim in Druid Lake. Large events and construction can redirect traffic, while zoo, conservatory and pool operations do not match general park access; follow current signs and operator alerts.

launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.summary: A 137-acre East Baltimore destination park with nearly three miles of paths, the Observatory, Boat Lake, two playgrounds, dog park, pool, ice rink, courts and athletic fields.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.hours: Park grounds are open daily from dawn to dusk. The Observatory is typically open Sundays from 11:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m. from mid-April through mid-October; pool, rink and recreation facilities keep separate seasonal hours.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.parking: There is no general visitor parking inside the park. Use legal street parking around the perimeter and read residential restrictions carefully; event days and pool season increase demand.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.arrival: Choose the Observatory and Boat Lake, playground, dog park, pool, rink or athletic fields before arriving. Baltimore Street, Linwood Avenue and Eastern Avenue serve different sides of the park.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.restrooms: Restrooms are most dependable at staffed or seasonal facilities such as the recreation center, pool and rink. Do not assume an outdoor restroom will be open early, late or off-season.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.cost: General park paths, playgrounds, dog park and outdoor landmarks are free. Pool, rink, classes, rentals and permitted activities may charge.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.accessibility: Many primary paths are paved and the park is relatively compact, but slopes, curb transitions and historic structures vary. Select the closest perimeter entrance for the feature you want.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.dogs: Dogs must be leashed outside the fenced dog park, with leashes no longer than six feet under posted rules. Dogs are excluded from pools, playgrounds and other posted facilities.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.family: Two playgrounds, Boat Lake, the Observatory and seasonal pool make a strong family circuit. Check the Observatory and pool schedule before promising entry.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.transit: MTA bus service runs along multiple park edges, including Baltimore Street and Eastern Avenue. Select the stop nearest your destination rather than the center of the park.
launch-md-baltimore-patterson-park.need: The Observatory is volunteer-staffed and weather-dependent, and seasonal facilities can close independently. Unauthorized motor vehicles are not permitted on park paths.

launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.summary: A compact historic hilltop park above the Inner Harbor with skyline overlooks, lawns, monuments, a history-themed playground and a lower basketball court.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.hours: Outdoor park areas are generally available from dawn to dusk, subject to events, maintenance and posted restrictions.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.parking: The park has no dependable dedicated visitor lot. Use legal neighborhood street parking or a paid Inner Harbor garage, and expect tighter availability during weekends, festivals and stadium events.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.arrival: For the least-steep approach, arrive from the Federal Hill neighborhood near Warren Avenue. The staircase from the harbor side is direct but steep.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom in the park. Use an open nearby business, museum or Inner Harbor visitor facility before climbing the hill.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.cost: Park access, overlooks, playground and monuments are free. Nearby garages, attractions, permits and events cost separately.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.accessibility: The upper plateau is largely level once reached, but the harbor-side staircase and surrounding grades are steep. Approach from Warren Avenue for the most practical step-free route.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor areas. There is no off-leash dog enclosure, and dogs should stay out of play equipment and posted event areas.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.family: The harbor view and ship-and-tower playground make a memorable short family stop. Closely supervise children around slopes, walls and busy bordering streets.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.transit: Charm City Circulator and MTA service reach the Inner Harbor and Federal Hill neighborhood, followed by an uphill walk. The promenade and nearby bike routes also connect to the area.
launch-md-baltimore-federal-hill-park.need: This is a viewpoint rather than a full-service park: bring water, plan a restroom stop and expect wind on the exposed summit. Fireworks and major events can radically change access.

launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.summary: The waterfront national monument where the defense of Baltimore inspired the national anthem, with a visitor center, Star Fort, historic batteries, seawall path, lawns and ranger programs.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.hours: Summer grounds open at 7:00 a.m. and close at 5:00 p.m. weekdays and 6:00 p.m. weekends; visitor center and Star Fort open at 9:00 a.m. Winter grounds are 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. Seasonal transitions and holiday closures apply, so confirm the NPS hours page.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.parking: Free parking is available onsite, including accessible spaces, but capacity is limited during peak seasons and major programs. Parking is for park visitors and cannot be used for unrelated all-day waterfront parking.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.arrival: Enter from East Fort Avenue and begin at the Paul S. Sarbanes Visitor and Education Center for orientation, current program times and Star Fort admission.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.restrooms: Accessible restrooms and water fountains are available at the visitor center during building hours. Facilities outside the staffed area are limited.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.cost: Most grounds, trails, visitor center and orientation film are free. Entry to the historic zone and Star Fort is $15 per adult age 16 and older, valid for seven days; the site is cashless and accepts federal passes.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.accessibility: Parking lots, visitor facilities, exhibits, restrooms and many paved routes are accessible. Wheelchairs are available to borrow, and exhibits include captioned and tactile resources.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed on outdoor grounds but not inside buildings or the historic Star Fort. Service animals are permitted in buildings under applicable rules.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.family: The orientation film, ranger talks, flag programs and Junior Ranger activity make this a strong family history visit. Program schedules vary, so check the calendar before arrival.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.transit: MTA bus service reaches the Locust Point area, but the final walk can be substantial. Bicycles are allowed on paved park areas but not inside the historic zone.
launch-md-baltimore-fort-mchenry-nationa.need: The Star Fort has shorter hours than the grounds. In summer, last park entry is 4:45 p.m. weekdays and 5:45 p.m. weekends; winter and fall last entry is 4:45 p.m. The park closes Thanksgiving, December 25 and January 1. Check NPS alerts before traveling.

launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.summary: A free 200-acre public arboretum with specimen trees, formal gardens, historic mansion, nature center, greenhouses, meadows and woodland walking trails.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.hours: Outdoor grounds are open Tuesday-Sunday, currently 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m., and closed Mondays. Building schedules change independently; the Nature Education Center and Mansion have limited posted hours, and the Vollmer Center is temporarily closed for maintenance.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.parking: Free onsite parking is available near the main entrance and Vollmer Center. Accessible spaces are in the upper lot; special events can change parking or use overflow areas.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.arrival: Use the main Greenspring Avenue gate and start near the Vollmer Center circle for maps and the most direct access to formal gardens. Gates close promptly, so leave enough time to return to your vehicle.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.restrooms: Restrooms are available in the Greenhouse Classroom during arboretum hours; staffed buildings provide additional facilities only when open.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.cost: General arboretum and garden entry is free. Classes, special events, rentals and permitted photography may charge.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.accessibility: Paved routes connect parking, major buildings and formal gardens, with accessible parking near Vollmer Center. Woodland trails have natural surfaces and are not recommended for strollers.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on outdoor grounds; clean-up bags are provided. Pets are not ordinarily allowed inside buildings, and service-animal rules apply.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.family: Gardens, the children's garden and Nature Education Center are family-friendly. Balls, lawn games, kites and climbing trees are prohibited to protect the collection.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.transit: MTA service runs near Greenspring Avenue, but the final approach and distances across the grounds should be checked before relying on transit.
launch-md-baltimore-cylburn-arboretum.need: There is no food service onsite. Picnics are limited to groups of ten or fewer, tables and tents are prohibited, and posed photography or proposals require advance permission.

launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.summary: Baltimore's largest woodland park, covering more than 1,000 acres with forest trails, the Gwynns Falls Trail, Carrie Murray Nature Center, historic estates, meadows and stream valleys.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.hours: Outdoor park areas are generally used from dawn to dusk. Carrie Murray Nature Center, Orianda Mansion, programs and special events have separate limited schedules; confirm before making them the purpose of a trip.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.parking: Parking is distributed among Windsor Mill Road, Carrie Murray Nature Center, Winans Meadow and smaller trailheads. Navigate to a named destination and do not leave valuables visible in a vehicle.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.arrival: The park is divided by roads, streams and steep wooded terrain. Choose Carrie Murray Nature Center, Winans Meadow, Crimea Estate or a specific Gwynns Falls Trail access point before departure.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.restrooms: Dependable restrooms are concentrated at Carrie Murray Nature Center and programmed facilities when open. Remote trails, meadows and historic sites may have no facilities.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.cost: General park and trail access are free. Programs, camps, reservations and permitted events may charge.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.accessibility: Carrie Murray Nature Center has a small paved approach with an accessible space, while most woodland trails include roots, mud, grades and uneven surfaces. The paved Gwynns Falls Trail is the most predictable route.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on ordinary park trails. Keep dogs controlled near wildlife, cyclists and equestrians, and follow restrictions at the nature center and historic buildings.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.family: Carrie Murray Nature Center and Winans Meadow are the easiest family anchors. Longer woodland routes require a downloaded map, sturdy footwear, water and close supervision.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.transit: MTA buses reach several surrounding neighborhoods, while the Gwynns Falls Trail connects by bicycle and foot. Service does not eliminate long distances inside the park.
launch-md-baltimore-gwynns-falls-leakin-.need: Cell coverage, signs and facilities vary in the wooded interior. Download a map, tell someone your route, avoid stream crossings during high water and leave enough daylight for the return.

launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.summary: Baltimore's public harbor-edge walking network linking the Inner Harbor, West Shore Park, Rash Field, Harbor East, Fells Point, Canton, playgrounds, piers and waterfront events.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.hours: The outdoor promenade is generally available daily, but individual parks, bridges, attractions, fountains and construction zones keep separate schedules or may close temporarily.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.parking: Use a paid garage near the portion you plan to visit; one parking location is not convenient for the entire waterfront. Read event rates and avoid assuming street spaces will be available.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.arrival: For a first visit, begin at the Baltimore Visitor Center at 401 Light Street. For playgrounds use Rash Field or Pierce's Park, and for Fells Point or Canton choose a closer eastern starting point.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.restrooms: Public restroom access is tied to the Visitor Center, staffed attractions and open businesses; there is no continuous chain of dependable outdoor facilities along the full route.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.cost: Walking the promenade and entering its public parks is free. Garages, Water Taxi, museums, attractions, food and ticketed events cost separately.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.accessibility: Most central promenade segments are paved and broadly level, but bridge transitions, construction detours, brick surfaces and crowded events can affect step-free travel.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on ordinary outdoor promenade segments and many parks. Attractions, fountains, play areas and events set separate restrictions.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.family: Rash Field's adventure play and skate park, West Shore Park's seasonal fountain and Pierce's Park are the strongest free child-focused stops. Water edges require continuous supervision.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.transit: Charm City Circulator, MTA bus and rail, bikeshare and the Water Taxi serve different waterfront sections. A one-way promenade walk can be paired with transit for the return.
launch-md-baltimore-baltimore-waterfront.need: The harbor is an active urban waterway, not a general swimming area. Rash Field Phase I remains open while Phase II construction creates detours; the new lawn, gardens, beach and paths are expected to open by the end of summer 2026. Check current Waterfront Partnership notices.

launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.summary: A 503-acre lake and nature park with forest, wetlands, serpentine barrens, a nature center, boardwalk, playground, pavilions, trails, paddling access and membership dog park.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.hours: Park grounds are open daily from sunrise to sunset. The Nature Center is generally open Tuesday-Sunday from 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; programs and seasonal operations vary.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.parking: Free parking is available at the Lakeside Drive lot and the Falls Road Light Rail lot. The light-rail lot connects to the park by a roughly 0.3-mile boardwalk and can be useful when the main lot is busy.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.arrival: Use Lakeside Drive for the Nature Center, playground and central trails, or Falls Road Light Rail for the boardwalk approach. Photograph the trail map before entering the wooded network.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.restrooms: The Nature Center provides the most dependable restrooms during building hours. Trail areas and Paw Point do not guarantee nearby year-round facilities.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.cost: General park, boardwalk and trail access are free. Programs may charge, and Paw Point is a code-controlled membership off-leash area with a separate annual fee.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.accessibility: A wheelchair-accessible boardwalk links the Falls Road Light Rail lot to the central park area. Natural trails include roots, rocks, mud and grades; use the paved central routes for the most predictable surface.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.dogs: Dogs must be leashed in the general park. Paw Point is a fenced membership-only off-leash swim-and-play area; water access can close independently based on testing or conditions.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.family: The boardwalk, Nature Center, playground and short central trails form the easiest family visit. Longer colored trails vary in surface and can become muddy after rain.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.transit: MTA Light RailLink stops at Falls Road, where a boardwalk leads directly into the park. This is one of the region's most practical transit-to-trail connections.
launch-md-baltimore-lake-roland-park.need: Check current water quality, Paw Point water access, lightning and park alerts before water-edge activities. Gates close at sunset, and natural trails can remain wet or icy after paved routes clear.
